question: Why does the caret fine-tuning loss start at ~0.78 and then rise to ~1.07 (C#, lr 2e-4), while quality improves?
method: completion-only loss of the language model BEFORE fine-tuning on 1 500-3 000 random training caret documents and on unseen eval-fresh positions, split into the <|endoftext|> stop token and the line tokens (tools: loss_probe.py on the H200 server)
rejected_hypothesis: memorisation of the training files (train vs unseen loss equal: 1.19 vs 1.19)
findings: A language model trained on whole files never sees <|endoftext|> right after a line: loss 3.6 on 10 % of the completion tokens. The fine-tuning learns it in the first ~100 steps -> the loss drops to ~0.7.
With lr 2e-4 the loss then rises to ~1.07: the line tokens get worse (noisy gradients: ~300 loss tokens per step). lr 5e-5 keeps it at ~0.7 and gives +3.3 p.p. exact (experiment 04).
On line tokens the new language model is already better than the shipped one (0.92 vs 0.94 on unseen positions).
